nodes.label: Pull-based auto-deploy poller
nodes.rationale: A poller sidecar watches the :prod tag in GHCR via skopeo inspect and reconciles the running image every 30 seconds, with a health gate and automatic rollback — pull-based so the VM needs no inbound CI access.

nodes.label: Merge gate IS the deploy gate
nodes.rationale: The pull-based design has no gate other than the main merge, so branch protection (required PR, required CI status check, block force pushes, enforce for administrators) is load-bearing — a bypass is a hole straight into production.

nodes.label: Deterministic GHCR authfile (.ghcr-auth.json)
nodes.rationale: The poller mounts a fixed path instead of ~/.docker/config.json, which is empty under sudo without -H or in systemd units where $HOME is unset. credStore caveat: if docker login used a credential helper there is no inline auth token, so skopeo gets 401 — write the base64 token explicitly.

nodes.label: HOLD sentinel file
nodes.rationale: /state/HOLD in the eps-poller-state volume pauses the poller. Set automatically on dependency fault, first-deploy image fault, or failed rollback; set manually during rollback because :prod still points at the bad digest and the poller would otherwise re-detect and redeploy it.

nodes.label: Health gate and automatic rollback
nodes.rationale: Gate polls /readyz up to 10 times with 3s delay, Redis checked in parallel. Distinguishes dependency fault (hold) from pure image fault (roll back to the previous running digest, `prev`), so no prior state is needed for rollback to work from the first deploy.

nodes.label: Seed deploy.env with the tag, not a digest
nodes.rationale: The poller pins the immutable digest on its first real deploy; seeding with the tag sidesteps multi-arch digest parsing and old-buildx --format incompatibility, which bit the first production bootstrap. Bootstrap is therefore never health-gated.

nodes.label: nginx must overwrite X-Real-IP
nodes.rationale: The backend's rate limiter trusts X-Real-IP for its per-client bucket, so appending rather than overwriting would let one caller spoof another caller's quota.

nodes.label: Same-origin /api rewrite over absolute backend URL
nodes.rationale: Routing /api through the site's own origin keeps session cookies first-party — no credentialed CORS, no preflight, no SameSite=None. Uses a Vercel `routes` entry (not `rewrites`) because only routes expand an env var, keeping the backend hostname out of the repo; ordering must beat the SPA catch-all. Without a real /api server, /api/me falls through to the SPA fallback and returns index.html with a 200, which once made /console render a fake signed-in user.

nodes.label: KV store redundancy tiers (Valkey / in-memory / Upstash)
nodes.rationale: Valkey container is the default (FOSS BSD Redis fork, same RESP, service keeps the name `redis` so REDIS_URL and compose assertions never change). In-memory degraded mode requires exactly one backend process. Upstash free tier is the managed option. The choice is deployment-time only; the backend never fails over at runtime.

nodes.label: KV_ENCRYPTION_KEY is a stable secret
nodes.rationale: It encrypts GitHub OAuth tokens and refresh-token claims at rest in Redis with AES-256-GCM. Rotating requires flushing rt:* and ghtoken:* and forcing re-authentication — not a routine redeploy operation.
